claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology is conducting replications of 50 papers in the field of cancer biology published between 2010 and 2012.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of 50 papers in the field of cancer biology published between 2010 and 2012.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the project scope.

claim: Kang et al. (2011) demonstrated the phenomenon of oncogene-induced cellular senescence after intrahepatic injection of NRAS.
source: In these experiments, Kang et al. (2011) demonstrate the phenomenon of oncogene-induced cellular senescence and immune-mediated clearance of senescent cells after intrahepatic injection of NRAS (Figures 2I, 3B, 3C, and 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the original Kang et al. 2011 study and references to specific figures.

claim: CD4+ T cells are specifically necessary for immunoclearance of senescent cells.

claim: Cellular senescence is a permanent state of proliferative arrest.
source: Cellular senescence—a permanent state of proliferative arrest—has been shown to be an important failsafe mechanism against tumor development in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as an established definition in the introduction.

claim: Cellular senescence is an important failsafe mechanism against tumor development in vivo.

claim: Aberrant activation of oncogenes can force normal cells into a senescent state of stable cell cycle arrest.
source: Aberrant activation of oncogenes can force normal cells into a senescent state of stable cell cycle arrest (Narita and Lowe, 2005).

claim: Senescence is often associated with a pre-malignant state.
source: Senescence is often associated with a pre-malignant state, and a wide range of cancers have been shown to harbor populations of senescent cells (Quintanilla et al., 1986; Braig et al., 2005; Collado et al., 2005; Bennecke et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: A wide range of cancers have been shown to harbor populations of senescent cells.

evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: There is an ongoing debate in the field of cancer biology about the phenomenon of 'immune surveillance'.
source: An ongoing debate in the field of cancer biology has been the phenomenon of 'immune surveillance', or the ability of the immune system to specifically identify and eliminate nascent pre-cancerous (e.g., senescent) cells before they can cause harm (Swann and Smyth, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Swann and Smyth, 2007 and describes the state of the field.

claim: Immune surveillance is the ability of the immune system to specifically identify and eliminate nascent pre-cancerous cells before they can cause harm.

evidence: This is a definition provided in the text with supporting citation.

claim: The possibility of tailored, pro-senescent therapies for cancer treatment has provoked considerable interest.
